entry.title: Multiband Compression: Definition and Use Cases
entry.content:
MusicTech | musictech.com

Multiband compressors divide an audio signal into several frequency bands—typically three to five—and apply independent compression settings to each before recombining them. This approach allows for targeted dynamic control of specific frequency ranges, such as the low end, without affecting the rest of the spectrum or causing audible pumping.

The technique is widely used in mixing and mastering to provide cohesion and tonal balance, functioning similarly to a broad-brushed equalizer. It is particularly effective when managing complex signals like full drum kits or synths where different frequency ranges require distinct dynamic responses.

entry.title: Understanding LUFS and Loudness Measurement in Music Production
entry.content:
MusicTech | musictech.com

LUFS (Loudness Units Full Scale) is a standardized method for measuring perceived audio loudness, primarily utilized during the mastering phase of music production. Unlike peak level meters that respond to sudden transients, LUFS accounts for the human ear's sensitivity to various frequencies, providing a consistent way to compare the loudness of different recordings.

Loudness is measured using four distinct metrics: Momentary, Short-Term, Integrated, and True Peak. These measurements are essential for meeting the specific integrated loudness and true peak specifications required by streaming platforms, which apply normalization to audio that does not adhere to their loudness standards.
